food: Realism.outbound_message (kernel/realism.py ~974): label rewriting runs one re.sub per name, one after another, over the whole message, including JSON inspect/read payloads that already carry perceived identity. Same knowledge-gated rule applied to open_mail, open_package (wrong address, former occupant, gift note, another resident's parcel), a neighbour's mailbox and reading a confidential paper or diary: refused generically only once the robot has read the label, otherwise a privacy violation. A private document keeps the kernel's generic wording.
Labels of unidentified things: need_tool and the label writer's 'Hold the ... first' now name the tool by id (handle).
Permanent marker look-alike: with a marker the robot has not identified, a permanent label is written in washable ink instead of refused; the old refusal identified the marker.
Refill spills are labelled by their look ('spilled liquid' / 'spilled dry goods') instead of the product name.
Shred: the duration is quantized to 5-sheet bulk (3 s per started 5 sheets), and the message and jam reason no longer count sheets hidden in an envelope.
Counts in messages: staple and collate give the eye's count (exact up to 12), and a bent staple gives no capacity numbers.

Refill: the pouring time now follows the amount rounded to 50 ml, the same precision as the message. Pouring grants inspect on both containers, so the soap look-alike groups resolve consistently with the viscosity-dependent time.
mount_roll: a refusal gives the eye's estimate ('about N%') instead of the exact remaining fraction.
Under-bed clearance: the realistic refusal gives no centimetres.

count: a closed opaque bottle or box is no longer reported as empty or partly used (its level shows 'unknown', full or not), and unresolved look-alikes are matched by the group's kind, not a member's category.

collate no longer echoes the true id of the stack it destroyed (a destroyed id passes the kernel's message translation untouched).

Documents: 'sheets' (pairs that include internal doc keys; a mail piece's key embeds the envelope's true id) is now hidden, and a new read-tier 'page_order' holds the printed page numbers. Pages without printed numbers hide 'in_order' through a per-entity _perception tier.

Furnisher: a child's backpack is labelled "child's backpack" with the child's first name on a read-tier name_label tag; before, its label showed the never-tier owner.
Look-alike groups now set descriptive 'candidates', a 'kind' and 'label_fields'. The black-bag group's candidates used to name its only member ('donation bag').
Mail type: sensitive, pii, shred_required and confidential are read-tier; piece_kind is hidden.
